# Prajnyavan (pj)

> Prajnyavan (binary name `pj`) is a local-first AI coding CLI, written in Rust, that runs agentic multi-step coding and debugging sessions against a local Ollama model by default, with optional escalation to a cloud provider (Anthropic or OpenAI). It includes real OS-level sandboxing (macOS Seatbelt / Linux bubblewrap) for command execution.

Prajnyavan's application source is closed and lives in a private repository. This
site and the `pj-releases` repo it's published from are the public surface of the
project: compiled binaries, install instructions, and documentation of what
currently works versus what's still scaffolded.

## Docs

- [Website](https://prajnyavan.github.io/pj-releases/): install instructions, feature list, architecture overview
- [Full text](https://prajnyavan.github.io/pj-releases/llms-full.txt): the entire site's content as plain text, for ingestion without HTML parsing
- [Releases](https://github.com/prajnyavan/pj-releases/releases): compiled binaries for macOS (arm64, x86_64) and Linux (x86_64), each with a `.sha256` checksum

## Notes

- Default local model: `qwen2.5-coder:7b` via Ollama. `pj doctor` warns if an installed model is too large for available RAM.
- Sandboxing (macOS Seatbelt, Linux bubblewrap) is real and enforced; the plugin system (WASM via `wasmtime`) and MCP (Model Context Protocol) support are scaffolded but not yet wired into the live agent loop, and say so explicitly rather than simulating success.
- `pj build` runs a generate → verify → fix loop: it scaffolds a project, runs its real build/test command, and asks the model to repair failures, with a bounded retry count.
